svg.title: SUN_MULTITIME file format
svg.text: Reverse-engineered from SunAcc42.c / SunAcc42.h (SunAcc v4.2.7.2, 4/17/2019) and the sample file test1.multi (518,492 bytes).
test1.multi starts with bytes FF FF FF F4, so it is the 64-bit variant (SUN_MULTITIME64). The 64-bit layout is drawn as the main layout; the 32-bit differences are shown next to it.

Top bar: the sample file, with real offsets (not to scale). Bottom bar: a typical file that contains data. Parameter data is a linked list of blocks per parameter. Blocks for different parameters are interleaved in the order they were written.
517,315 B: leftover of the reserved comment space (99.8% of the file)
test1.multi: every map entry has blockPtr = 0, so the file contains NO data blocks. Because parameter 0's blockPtr is 0, the reader treats everything from the end of the map to EOF

(517,976 B) as the comment block (SunAcc42.c:1194-1197). The file size is 264 + 5 x 1038 + commentBlockSZ, with commentBlockSZ = 513,038 (inferred): the reserved comment area was copied down to the end of the map at close and the tail was left in place.
linked (absolute offset of the next block for the same parameter; 0 = end of chain)

How the writer creates this: createSunFile() writes a 264-byte zero header, reserves nItems x 1038 bytes for the map (filled with 0x20) and commentBlockSZ bytes for comments (filled with 0x00), and writes data blocks after that.

closeSunFile() copies the comment block down to the end of the real map. Only SUN_MULTITIME (32-bit) is packed (gap removed), and only when the gap is larger than 8 KB and no appends were recorded. MULTITIME64 and _SRT files keep the gap.
2. File header: 264 bytes at offset 0 (SunAcc42.h struct SunHeader). Every integer is BE.
Format signature, see table at right. Stays 0 until every map entry is written.
Reference year (stored, but ignored by the time math)
Reference Julian day (0 is read as 1)
Millisecond. Relative time 0 is this moment, unless a FILE_REF event overrides it.
Number of parameters / map entries. Stays 0 until the map is complete.
Set equal to [1] on close. [0] != [1] means the file is still being written (live).
Update counter: +1 per append or showFileUpdated() call
Fixed-width text, NUL padded, not necessarily NUL terminated
The parameter map starts at offset 264, a value hard-coded in several places
bytes on disk are always FF FF FF Fx (effectively BE).
_SRT = server-backed real time. On open it is
closeSrtFile() rewrites the signature to the plain form.
1. Header written with sig = 0 and items = 0.
2. When the last map entry is written,
items and then sig are written, and the file
3. Each append: link the previous block,
Readers poll with refreshSunFile(), which re-reads
bytes 0-39 and compares sig, refTime, items, counters.
3. Parameter map: N variable-length entries packed from offset 264 (format of struct VarNomenMap)
Each string has a 1-byte length prefix (0-255), with no NUL and no padding. The example is test1.multi entry 0, at offsets 264-314.
blockPtr: i64 BE offset of first block (0 = no data)

32-bit SUN_MULTITIME: blockPtr is 2 x u32 BE (blockPtr[0] = first block, blockPtr[1] always 0), so the entry length is the same. Entry size = 4 + sum(string lengths) + 2 + 4 + 8, at most 1038 bytes, which is also the space the writer reserves per entry.
If bit 31 is set, rate = (seqNum >> 16) & 0x7FFF (PACK_RATE macro).
A [rates] comment section can also set a rate. Both set bit 31 (enables makeFullRate).
4. Comment block: free text from the end of the map up to blockPtr of parameter 0 (or EOF)
INI-like sections found with strstr(). The DLL parses only [events], [rates] and [extendednomen]. Other sections, such as [coef] in test1.multi, belong to the application and the DLL ignores them.
File events (max 4096). If the day is not 1-366, '(invalid)' is appended to the name.
Overrides the header reference time (relative t = 0)
Last value is held until this time on reads
Sets parameter rate and seqNum bit 31
Third name and second description per parameter
...then 517,315 zero bytes to EOF (the reader treats them as comment too).
5. Parameter data: a singly linked chain of blocks per parameter (none are present in test1.multi)
map.blockPtr gives the first block. Each block header's 'linked' field gives the absolute offset of the next block for the same parameter.
Appending data writes a new block at EOF and patches the previous block's link (at blockAddr + 4), or the map blockPtr if the parameter had no data yet.
block 1 (first): carries index nomen if nomenSize>0
Uncompressed (compressed = 0): time array, then data array, as raw values. The reader seeks to dataStart + points*iSz + startPoint*dSz, so it can read a sub-range without reading the whole block.

Compressed (compressed = 1): an LZH stream of TimeLzhSize bytes followed directly by an LZH stream of DataLzhSize bytes (ar002 / -lh5-, 8 KB dictionary). Time values are delta-coded before compression (except u4). Any read decodes from the start of the block.

nomenSize > 0 (first block only): 'name,units,description' CSV text for the time/index axis. It is stored without a NUL. points = number of samples. The type of each time value is set by indexType, and the type of each data value by the map type ID.
6. Block header (pidHeader64 / pidHeader). Each field is read and written separately (no struct padding on disk) and is always BE.
iT = indexType (u8) nS = nomenSize (u8) cp = compressed (u8, 0/1) BE = bigEndian (u8, 0/1)
bigEndian (byte 23/19) sets the byte order of the time and data ARRAYS only. The writer defaults to host order; the ORIENT_BIG_END / ORIENT_LITTLE_END / ORIENT_NATIVE options override it.
For 'v1' (variable-size) blocks, TimeLzhSize (and DataLzhSize when uncompressed) holds the blob size in bytes. The single time stamp is never compressed, even when compressed = 1.
An in-memory field, blkBaseUTC (the TimeTag of firstTime), is NOT stored on disk. The reader rebuilds it, and packed-time decoding uses it as the base day.
7. Index (time) encodings and data value types
{u32 ms-of-day, u16 us, i16 JulianDay} each field swapped
u32: bits 31-27 rel. day (vs block firstTime), 26-0 ms
Data value types (ASCII ID in map entry; size = 2nd char - '0')
Always BE: header integers and float, map length/seqNum/blockPtr, every pidHeader field
(including firstTime/lastTime; a TimeTag is swapped field by field).
Per-block flag: time and data arrays (bigEndian byte).
A t8 value used as INDEX is swapped field by field. A t8 value used as DATA is reversed as one
8-byte unit. In a BE block the two have different byte layouts.
Map type IDs: the first char is lower-cased on read. The map uses ASCII IDs while pidHeader
uses numeric DT codes. indexType 9 is produced only by PACK_TIMETAG on a t8 index.
A missing sample is stored as 0x80000001 (DROP_OUT) / FP_DROP_OUT for 4-byte types.
8. Issues, limitations, security risks and idiosyncrasies
Line numbers refer to SunAcc42.c. For each defect, the 64-bit reader/writer functions duplicate the 32-bit code and share the same problem.
Signature FF FF FF F4 = SUN_MULTITIME64, not 32-bit SUN_MULTITIME. Reference = 2010 day 175 00:00:50.513, 5 parameters (all 'd8', seqNum 1, no rate flag), blockPoints 1/1 (closed, not live).
Every map blockPtr is 0: the file holds NO data blocks. readSunParm() on any parameter returns ERR_TIMESLICE after re-reading the map pointer.
517,315 of 518,492 bytes (99.8%) are zero fill. The reader takes the whole region from offset 516 to EOF (517,976 B) as the comment block, because parameter 0 has no data block.
The [events] section has EOF=175/0.0 and ALIGN=175/0.0, both 50.513 s BEFORE the file reference time. The [coef] section (MSID/COEF records) belongs to the application and is not parsed by SunAcc.
The comment text ends with two lines of 125 spaces each (reserved editing space).
SECURITY RISKS / DEFECTS CONFIRMED IN THE CODE (exploitable with a crafted or corrupt file)
Static buffer overflows in the ar002 LZH decoder. read_pt_len(NT=19, TBIT=5) accepts a count n up to 31, plus up to 3 zero-run entries, and writes into pt_len[19]. read_c_len() accepts n up to 511
and zero-runs up to 531 entries, and writes into c_len[510] (SunAcc42.c:9119-9225, arrays at 9034-9035). Any compressed block can therefore corrupt global memory. This is the same class of bug as the
32-bit size arithmetic on fields read from the file: malloc(pHead->points * bsize) (3439, 64-bit path ~4075), malloc(bufAllocSz * DataTypeSize) (3766) and the 64-bit equivalents can wrap.
lzh_decode()/fread() then write points*iSz bytes into the short buffer (heap overflow). For 'v1' blocks, DataTypeSize = 4 + TimeLzhSize, which comes straight from the file. The element size
(typeIDS[1] - '0') is never validated; e.g. ID 'f' + 0x00 gives 0xFFFFFFD0.
Out-of-bounds reads in STRNDUP(), which calls strlen() before applying maxlen. retrieveFileMap() passes sBuf[256], which is never NUL-terminated and is stale or uninitialized when a length byte is 0
(920-935). openSunFile() passes the fixed char[80]/char[12] header fields (1155-1161). testNumber is the last member of the heap-allocated SunHeader, so a full 12-character value reads past the
No validation of the header 'items' count or of fread() results in retrieveFileMap(). A large items value (in the millions, so calloc still succeeds) on a short file loops items times, allocating
strings (DoS). refreshSunFile() reloads the map the same way.
The 'linked' chain has no cycle or bounds check. A link that points back to an earlier block makes readMultiTimeParm(64) grow its address stack by 32 entries per pass until realloc fails (memory
Comment-block size is computed only from parameter 0's first blockPtr (1182-1201). If parameter 0 has no data, everything up to EOF, including other parameters' binary blocks, is parsed as comment
text. If blockPtr < commentOffset, the unsigned subtraction wraps (it is clamped to 64 MB). commentOffset comes from 32-bit ftell() even for 64-bit files.
Wrong byte-swap test for variable blocks. The reader tests typeIDS[1] != 'v' (always true) instead of typeIDS[0] (3817 and the 64-bit copy). When a block's bigEndian flag differs from the host, it
byte-reverses the opaque 'v1' blob, or the FP_VARIABLE sentinel, as one unit. The writer never swaps 'v1' data.
setCommentText() saves the file position in savePos64 for 64-bit files but restores it from the uninitialized 32-bit savePos (7689). This is an undefined-behavior read and a wrong position restore.
It is currently masked because every library write path seeks before it writes.
closeSunFile() packs a 32-bit file when blockPoints[1] == 0. Blocks appended with MANUAL_UPDATE, without a call to showFileUpdated(), leave the counter at 0. Packing then moves the data and fixes the
map pointers, but not the absolute 'linked' offsets inside the block headers, so the chain is corrupted.
createSunFile(): mapEstAdj = (writeMode >> 8) && 0x0007 is computed after writeMode &= 0x000F, so it is always 0 (logical && instead of &). The MAP20-MAP80 pre-allocation options documented in
closeSunFile() packing runs pBlk[0] -= packSpace without checking for 0 (8710); only pBlk[1] is guarded. A parameter added with no data (blockPtr 0) gets a wrapped pointer of about 0xFFFFxxxx. Reads
then fail with ERR_LINK_HDR_RD instead of 'no data', and if it is parameter 0 the comment size wraps, so events are lost. This affects only packed 32-bit files (gap > 8 KB, about 9+ parameters).
test1.multi (64-bit, never packed) is not affected, although every one of its pointers is NULL.
Not thread-safe or re-entrant: global accError/wrtError, global LZH decoder state, and strtok() in comment parsing. The TRUNCATE(a,b) macro ignores its arguments and uses the variable sPtr.
make_table() indexes count[bitlen[i]] (count[17]) without checking bitlen <= 16. The pt_len escape loop can produce longer lengths, which would overflow a stack array.
A block with points = 0 gives malloc(0), but the reader still accesses time[0] and data[points-1] (points-1 wraps to 0xFFFFFFFF).
The two compressed streams are read back to back with no fseek() to the data stream. Correctness relies on the time decoder consuming exactly TimeLzhSize bytes, and a truncated stream is padded with
zero bits instead of being reported as an error.
On a big-endian host, packed-time arrays use FLIP() (a no-op there) instead of flip(), so little-endian packed times are not swapped. Every other index type handles this case.
The reader finds a block header again by subtracting PHEAD(64)SIZE from the stored data start. This works only because nomen bytes appear in the first block alone, whose address comes from the map.
A live writer publishes a zeroed header first and patches it later. fflush() is skipped under MANUAL_UPDATE, so a polling reader can see a link or counter that points at an unflushed block.
SUN_MULTITIME stores u32 offsets but seeks with fseek(long), which is effectively 2 GB on Windows. MULTITIME64 removes that limit for offsets, but block-internal sizes (points*iSz, startPoint*dSz)
and the comment offset and size are still 32-bit.
Time is returned as float32 relative seconds whatever the stored precision: about 7.8 ms resolution 1 day from the reference and about 2 s after 1 year. Float index deltas are themselves float32, so
rounding error accumulates over long blocks.
No year arithmetic: TIME() assumes |day difference| < 180 and 365-day years, and UTC() clamps offsets to +/-180 days and wraps day > 365 with % 365, which mishandles leap years. The header year is
DT_ULONGINT index: milliseconds since the file reference, at most 49.7 days, and never delta-coded. DT_PACKEDTIME: a 5-bit relative day where a wrap is detected only when the day decreases, so a gap
of 32 days or more inside one block is ambiguous. Microseconds are discarded.
Map strings and the index nomen are at most 255 bytes each. Nomen is stored only in a parameter's first block. UPDATE mode can append data but cannot add parameters. Events are capped at 4096 and the
Element size comes from a single ASCII digit, so types are limited to 1-9 bytes. Sub-range reads of compressed blocks must decompress from the start of the block.
Byte order is mixed: structural fields are always BE, while the arrays follow a per-block flag that defaults to host order. The signature is compared as a native u32 against platform-specific
Header fields are reused for other purposes. blockPoints[0..1] act as an update counter and an end-of-writing flag. TimeLzhSize/DataLzhSize hold the blob size for 'v1'. The top 16 bits of seqNum hold
a rate flag and value. The firstTime/lastTime slots are 8 bytes read as float, u32, double or TimeTag depending on indexType.
Type codes appear in two forms: ASCII IDs in the map ('d8', first char lower-cased on read) and numeric DT codes in pidHeader. 'p4' is a legal map data ID, but indexType 9 (packed time) is produced
only by the PACK_TIMETAG option on a 't8' index.
Disk space reserved by the writer (1038 B per map entry, filled with 0x20, plus commentBlockSZ filled with 0x00) is never reclaimed for MULTITIME64 or _SRT files. Readers see the leftover space as
part of the comment block, as in test1.multi.
Header text fields are fixed-width and need not be NUL-terminated. STRNDUP turns empty strings into a single space (" ").
A FILE_REF event in the comment text silently replaces the header reference time. An EOF event makes reads repeat the last value up to that time.
Generated from SunAcc42.c/.h source analysis and a byte-level parse of test1.multi.
svg.desc:
PLAIN-TEXT COPY OF SECTION 8 (issues, limitations, security risks, idiosyncrasies)
SAMPLE FILE (test1.multi) OBSERVATIONS F1. Signature FF FF FF F4 = SUN_MULTITIME64, not 32-bit SUN_MULTITIME. Reference = 2010 day 175 00:00:50.513, 5 parameters (all 'd8', seqNum 1, no rate flag), blockPoints 1/1 (closed, not live). F2. Every map blockPtr is 0: the file holds NO data blocks. readSunParm() on any parameter returns ERR_TIMESLICE after re-reading the map pointer. F3. 517,315 of 518,492 bytes (99.8%) are zero fill. The reader takes the whole region from offset 516 to EOF (517,976 B) as the comment block, because parameter 0 has no data block. F4. The [events] section has EOF=175/0.0 and ALIGN=175/0.0, both 50.513 s BEFORE the file reference time. The [coef] section (MSID/COEF records) belongs to the application and is not parsed by SunAcc. The comment text ends with two lines of 125 spaces each (reserved editing space).
SECURITY RISKS / DEFECTS CONFIRMED IN THE CODE (exploitable with a crafted or corrupt file) S1. Static buffer overflows in the ar002 LZH decoder. read_pt_len(NT=19, TBIT=5) accepts a count n up to 31, plus up to 3 zero-run entries, and writes into pt_len[19]. read_c_len() accepts n up to 511 and zero-runs up to 531 entries, and writes into c_len[510] (SunAcc42.c:9119-9225, arrays at 9034-9035). Any compressed block can therefore corrupt global memory. This is the same class of bug as the published gzip/LHA unlzh decoder flaws. S2. 32-bit size arithmetic on fields read from the file: malloc(pHead->points * bsize) (3439, 64-bit path ~4075), malloc(bufAllocSz * DataTypeSize) (3766) and the 64-bit equivalents can wrap. lzh_decode()/fread() then write points*iSz bytes into the short buffer (heap overflow). For 'v1' blocks, DataTypeSize = 4 + TimeLzhSize, which comes straight from the file. The element size (typeIDS[1] - '0') is never validated; e.g. ID 'f' + 0x00 gives 0xFFFFFFD0. S3. Out-of-bounds reads in STRNDUP(), which calls strlen() before applying maxlen. retrieveFileMap() passes sBuf[256], which is never NUL-terminated and is stale or uninitialized when a length byte is 0 (920-935). openSunFile() passes the fixed char[80]/char[12] header fields (1155-1161). testNumber is the last member of the heap-allocated SunHeader, so a full 12-character value reads past the allocation. S4. No validation of the header 'items' count or of fread() results in retrieveFileMap(). A large items value (in the millions, so calloc still succeeds) on a short file loops items times, allocating strings (DoS). refreshSunFile() reloads the map the same way. S5. The 'linked' chain has no cycle or bounds check. A link that points back to an earlier block makes readMultiTimeParm(64) grow its address stack by 32 entries per pass until realloc fails (memory exhaustion). S6. Comment-block size is computed only from parameter 0's first blockPtr (1182-1201). If parameter 0 has no data, everything up to EOF, including other parameters' binary blocks, is parsed as comment text. If blockPtr < commentOffset, the unsigned subtraction wraps (it is clamped to 64 MB). commentOffset comes from 32-bit ftell() even for 64-bit files. S7. Wrong byte-swap test for variable blocks. The reader tests typeIDS[1] != 'v' (always true) instead of typeIDS[0] (3817 and the 64-bit copy). When a block's bigEndian flag differs from the host, it byte-reverses the opaque 'v1' blob, or the FP_VARIABLE sentinel, as one unit. The writer never swaps 'v1' data. S8. setCommentText() saves the file position in savePos64 for 64-bit files but restores it from the uninitialized 32-bit savePos (7689). This is an undefined-behavior read and a wrong position restore. It is currently masked because every library write path seeks before it writes. S9. closeSunFile() packs a 32-bit file when blockPoints[1] == 0. Blocks appended with MANUAL_UPDATE, without a call to showFileUpdated(), leave the counter at 0. Packing then moves the data and fixes the map pointers, but not the absolute 'linked' offsets inside the block headers, so the chain is corrupted. S10. createSunFile(): mapEstAdj = (writeMode >> 8) && 0x0007 is computed after writeMode &= 0x000F, so it is always 0 (logical && instead of &). The MAP20-MAP80 pre-allocation options documented in SunAcc42.h do nothing. S11. closeSunFile() packing runs pBlk[0] -= packSpace without checking for 0 (8710); only pBlk[1] is guarded. A parameter added with no data (blockPtr 0) gets a wrapped pointer of about 0xFFFFxxxx. Reads then fail with ERR_LINK_HDR_RD instead of 'no data', and if it is parameter 0 the comment size wraps, so events are lost. This affects only packed 32-bit files (gap > 8 KB, about 9+ parameters). test1.multi (64-bit, never packed) is not affected, although every one of its pointers is NULL. S12. Not thread-safe or re-entrant: global accError/wrtError, global LZH decoder state, and strtok() in comment parsing. The TRUNCATE(a,b) macro ignores its arguments and uses the variable sPtr.
POTENTIAL ISSUES (likely, not exercised here) P1. make_table() indexes count[bitlen[i]] (count[17]) without checking bitlen <= 16. The pt_len escape loop can produce longer lengths, which would overflow a stack array. P2. A block with points = 0 gives malloc(0), but the reader still accesses time[0] and data[points-1] (points-1 wraps to 0xFFFFFFFF). P3. The two compressed streams are read back to back with no fseek() to the data stream. Correctness relies on the time decoder consuming exactly TimeLzhSize bytes, and a truncated stream is padded with zero bits instead of being reported as an error. P4. On a big-endian host, packed-time arrays use FLIP() (a no-op there) instead of flip(), so little-endian packed times are not swapped. Every other index type handles this case. P5. The reader finds a block header again by subtracting PHEAD(64)SIZE from the stored data start. This works only because nomen bytes appear in the first block alone, whose address comes from the map. P6. A live writer publishes a zeroed header first and patches it later. fflush() is skipped under MANUAL_UPDATE, so a polling reader can see a link or counter that points at an unflushed block.
FORMAT LIMITATIONS L1. SUN_MULTITIME stores u32 offsets but seeks with fseek(long), which is effectively 2 GB on Windows. MULTITIME64 removes that limit for offsets, but block-internal sizes (points*iSz, startPoint*dSz) and the comment offset and size are still 32-bit. L2. Time is returned as float32 relative seconds whatever the stored precision: about 7.8 ms resolution 1 day from the reference and about 2 s after 1 year. Float index deltas are themselves float32, so rounding error accumulates over long blocks. L3. No year arithmetic: TIME() assumes |day difference| < 180 and 365-day years, and UTC() clamps offsets to +/-180 days and wraps day > 365 with % 365, which mishandles leap years. The header year is ignored. L4. DT_ULONGINT index: milliseconds since the file reference, at most 49.7 days, and never delta-coded. DT_PACKEDTIME: a 5-bit relative day where a wrap is detected only when the day decreases, so a gap of 32 days or more inside one block is ambiguous. Microseconds are discarded. L5. Map strings and the index nomen are at most 255 bytes each. Nomen is stored only in a parameter's first block. UPDATE mode can append data but cannot add parameters. Events are capped at 4096 and the comment block at 64 MB. L6. Element size comes from a single ASCII digit, so types are limited to 1-9 bytes. Sub-range reads of compressed blocks must decompress from the start of the block.
FORMAT IDIOSYNCRASIES I1. Byte order is mixed: structural fields are always BE, while the arrays follow a per-block flag that defaults to host order. The signature is compared as a native u32 against platform-specific constants. I2. Header fields are reused for other purposes. blockPoints[0..1] act as an update counter and an end-of-writing flag. TimeLzhSize/DataLzhSize hold the blob size for 'v1'. The top 16 bits of seqNum hold a rate flag and value. The firstTime/lastTime slots are 8 bytes read as float, u32, double or TimeTag depending on indexType. I3. Type codes appear in two forms: ASCII IDs in the map ('d8', first char lower-cased on read) and numeric DT codes in pidHeader. 'p4' is a legal map data ID, but indexType 9 (packed time) is produced only by the PACK_TIMETAG option on a 't8' index. I4. Disk space reserved by the writer (1038 B per map entry, filled with 0x20, plus commentBlockSZ filled with 0x00) is never reclaimed for MULTITIME64 or _SRT files. Readers see the leftover space as part of the comment block, as in test1.multi. I5. Header text fields are fixed-width and need not be NUL-terminated. STRNDUP turns empty strings into a single space (" "). I6. A FILE_REF event in the comment text silently replaces the header reference time. An EOF event makes reads repeat the last value up to that time.
